chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It was so that Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) was frequently saying in his sermons: 'O you people! Your Religion is your Religion, So the evil deed in it is better than the good deed in other (Religions), and the evil deed in it would be Forgiven, and the good deed in the other (Religions) would not be Accepted'.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: Why is a bad deed in Islam better than a good deed in another religion?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) articulates the principle of 'Salihiyyat al-Din' (excellence of the religion), asserting that the validity of the faith framework determines the acceptance of individual deeds. He teaches that a sin within Islam is expiated and forgiven, whereas a good deed performed in disbelief (Kufr) is rejected, highlighting the foundational role of correct creed (Aqidah) in Shia theology. This concept underscores that while actions are judged within the context of faith, the rejection of faith itself nullifies the spiritual merit of any good work.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Al Rayyan Bin Al Salt, raising it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘It was so that Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was frequently saying in his<sup>asws</sup> sermons: ‘O you people! Your Religion is your Religion, So the evil deed in it is better than the good deed in other (Religions), and the evil deed in it would be Forgiven, and the good deed in the other (Religions) would not be Accepted’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt in a marfu’ manner from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) would very often say about sin, ‘O people, pay attention to your religion, pay attention to your religion. An evil deed in it (your religion) is better than a good deed in something else. An evil deed in your religion can be forgiven (by means of repenting) but a good deed in something else will not be accepted.’”
